newsitem.title: UK: UK gas to Neds to break Gasunie pipe monopoly.
newsitem.headline: UK gas to Neds to break Gasunie pipe monopoly.

text.p: Gas from the British North Sea will be delivered to an end user in the Netherlands through the first independent pipeline in the country, breaking the monopoly of supplier Gasunie, a spokesman for the buyer said on Tuesday.

Leendert Florusse, project manager of EnTrade, one of the parties in the Elsta cogeneration plant being built in Terneuzen, south west Netherlands, said the plant's buying consortium, Inkoopcombinatie Elsta VOF, will start construction of a new 50 km plant next February. It will transport gas from the Belgian border as far as Bergen op Zoom and will be ready by October 1998.
From that date, Elsta will take one billion cubic metres (bcm) a year of gas from Centrica plc through the UK-ContinentInterconnector link.
Centrica and the Elsta consortium announced on Tuesday morning that they have agreed a deal for the delivery of the gas.
A spokesman for Centrica would not comment on the value of the deal except to say that it is "broadly in line with other continental deals."
Centrica will deliver the gas as far as Zeebrugge in Belgium, the landing point for the Interconnector which starts at Bacton on the east coast of England.

From there, Florusse said, the Elsta consortium will deliver gas through the infrastructure of Belgian distributor Distrigaz. He added that it is already possible for anyone transporting over 200 million cubic metres a year to strike a transportation agreement with Distrigaz.
The pipeline is planned to extend beyond Terneuzen to Bergen op Zoom.

Florusse said the consortium aimed to transport gas for other users in the area as well as for its own purposes. He agreed that the project would set a precedent in the Netherlands and could be influential in the final form of the EU's gas directive, expected to be finalised this year. "It clearly shows the direction in which the industry is going," he said.
The 406 MW cogeneration plant is on the site of the Dow Benelux chemical complex. It is jointly owned by AES Electric (50 percent), PNEM (25 percent) and DELTA (25 percent).
DELTA and PNEM, of which EnTrade is the trading affiliate, are multi-utility companies supplying the Dutch provinces of Zeeland and Noord-Brabant respectively.
Inkoopcombinatie Elsta VOF, the purchaser of gas from Centrica, unites PNEM, DELTA and Dow Dow Chemical Co.
